news.headline: Trump Orders Warning Signs Placed Outside Smithsonian History Museum, Accusing It of Inaccuracy
news.summary: トランプ大統領は内務省に対し、スミソニアン国立アメリカ歴史博物館の正面に「不正確な展示をしている」と非難する看板を設置するよう命じた。

commentary: 矛盾: 政府が公金で運営する国立博物館の「正確さ」を、同じ政府が外部から看板で否定するという、自己矛盾した構図になっている。
滑稽さ: 150年以上の歴史を持つ博物館を「不正確」と断じる手段が、玄関先に手書き風の看板を置くという、極めてアナログな抗議手法であることが際立っている。
日本・海外から見ると: 国立の歴史機関の展示内容を現政権が公式に「嘘だ」と宣言する国として、民主主義の先進国アメリカが海外に映る姿は複雑だろう。
imagePrompts: A grand neoclassical museum facade with a large handwritten-style government sign planted on the front lawn reading 'WARNING: MAY CONTAIN HISTORY'; tourists in line staring at the sign with puzzled expressions

A museum security guard in uniform standing next to an official-looking placard that contradicts the exhibit visible through the glass door behind him; the exhibit shows a historical artifact with a detailed label
An aerial view of a government building on one side and a museum on the other, connected by a giant arrow pointing in both directions labeled 'FUNDED BY' and 'NOT ACCURATE, SAYS FUNDER'
captions: The government has finally solved the problem of Americans not trusting institutions — by posting a sign telling them not to trust this institution.
Nothing says 'we value accurate history' like the administration ordering a sign that skips the peer review process entirely.
The Smithsonian has weathered the Civil War, two World Wars, and the disco era. The yard sign era may prove the most challenging.
It's a bold strategy: funding a museum for 150 years and then putting a sticky note on the door saying 'don't believe everything you read in there.'
Historians will note this as the first time in American history that a museum's most controversial exhibit was installed by the government, on the outside of the building.
captionsJa: アメリカ国民が「機関を信用しない」問題を解決した政府の答えは、「この機関を信用するな」という看板を立てることだった。
「正確な歴史を大切にします」という姿勢を示す方法として、査読も専門家も飛ばして看板を発注するのはなかなか大胆だ。
スミソニアンは南北戦争も二度の世界大戦もディスコ時代も乗り越えてきた。「看板の時代」が最大の試練になるとは誰も予想しなかっただろう。
150年間博物館に資金を出し続けておいて、入口に「中の展示は信用するな」というメモを貼るのは、なかなか豪快なスタイルだ。
歴史家たちは後世にこう記録するだろう。「ある博物館の最も物議を醸した展示物は、建物の外に政府が設置した看板だった」と。
candidates.newsEn: President Trump ordered the Interior Department to display signs in front of the Smithsonian National Museum of American History accusing the institution of inaccuracy. The order escalates the administration's ongoing campaign against what it characterizes as ideologically biased presentations of American history. The Smithsonian is a federally funded institution that has operated for over 150 years as the nation's premier public archive of American heritage.

ironyEn.contradiction: The federal government is using taxpayer money to post signs outside a federally funded institution telling the public not to trust that federally funded institution.
ironyEn.absurdity: After 150 years of curating the nation's history, the museum's most prominent new exhibit is apparently a government sign questioning whether any of it is true.
ironyEn.outside: Visitors from abroad who came to learn about American democracy may leave having witnessed a live demonstration of something else entirely.

ironyEn.contradiction: An administration that controls the institution's funding has decided the most effective rebuttal to its historians is… a yard sign.
ironyEn.absurdity: The Smithsonian has survived world wars and political upheaval — its newest challenge is apparently a placard from the Interior Department.
ironyEn.outside: Foreign observers accustomed to governments rewriting history books must be relieved to learn America has opted for the more transparent approach of posting sticky notes on the door.

news.headline: Trump Administration Admits Denying $7.5 Billion in Clean Energy Grants Based on States' Voting Records
news.summary: トランプ政権は、連邦のクリーンエネルギー補助金75億ドル超を、州がトランプ再選を支持したかどうかを基準に打ち切っていたことを法廷文書で認めた。

commentary: 矛盾: 連邦補助金は本来すべての州の納税者の税金で賄われるが、その分配が選挙の投票結果によって決まるという、「全国民のための政府」という建前と真逆の仕組みが法廷文書で明らかになった。
滑稽さ: 政権側は「誤った表現だ」と反論しながら、その「誤った表現」の内容を事実として法廷文書に記載しているという、自己否定的な弁明になっている。
日本・海外から見ると: 国家予算の配分が支持政党によって左右される構図は、先進民主主義国の制度的中立性という観点から、国際社会に強いメッセージを送ることになる。
imagePrompts: A giant vending machine labeled 'Federal Grants' dispensing money into some states' slots while other states' slots are covered with 'OUT OF ORDER' stickers shaped like voting ballots

A bureaucrat at a desk sorting grant application folders into two piles: one pile labeled 'APPROVED' with a green checkmark, another labeled 'WRONG ANSWER' with a red X; both piles have identical clean energy project descriptions on top

A courtroom scene where a document on the evidence stand clearly reads the policy criteria, while a lawyer at the podium holds a sign saying 'THIS IS A MISREPRESENTATION'; the judge and jury stare at the document
captions: Good news: the administration found a simple, merit-based system for distributing federal grants. Bad news: the merit in question was electoral.
The government has discovered a powerful new incentive for clean energy adoption — it's called voting correctly.
In a stunning breakthrough, scientists have discovered that solar panels in blue states produce less energy than previously thought — at least according to the grant office.
'It's a misrepresentation,' said the administration, in a document that represents exactly what they said it doesn't.
All 50 states' taxpayers funded the grants. Thirty-ish states' taxpayers got to keep them. Math, as always, remains non-partisan.
captionsJa: 朗報：政権は連邦補助金のシンプルで公正な配分基準を見つけた。悲報：その基準は「選挙結果」だった。
クリーンエネルギー普及のための新しい強力なインセンティブが発見された。「正しく投票すること」だ。
衝撃の研究結果：ブルーステートの太陽光パネルは、補助金窓口の計算上、発電量が著しく低いことが判明した。
「それは誤った表現だ」と政権は主張した。その主張を記した法廷文書には、誤りとされた内容がそのまま書いてあった。
50州の納税者全員が補助金を出した。受け取れたのはおよそ半分の州だった。数学だけは、相変わらず党派に忖度しない。
candidates.newsEn: Court filings reveal that the Trump administration canceled more than $7.5 billion in federal grants for clean energy projects to states based solely on whether those states had supported Trump's re-election. The administration acknowledged the criterion in legal documents but characterized criticism of the practice as a 'misrepresentation.' A dozen states had challenged the grant cancellations in court.

ironyEn.contradiction: Federal grants — funded by taxpayers in all 50 states regardless of how they vote — were apparently distributed based on which states voted the right way.
ironyEn.absurdity: The administration's defense against the accusation of political targeting was to confirm it in writing in a court document while calling the description a 'misrepresentation.'
ironyEn.outside: Countries that have long been lectured by the U.S. about the importance of keeping public funds out of politics now have a federal court filing to reference.

ironyEn.contradiction: Clean energy grants meant to benefit the environment were cancelled — but only in the environments that didn't vote correctly.
ironyEn.absurdity: Calling the documented policy a 'misrepresentation' while the documentation sits in the court record is a legal strategy that future law school classes will study for entirely different reasons.
ironyEn.outside: For a government that champions free markets, making $7.5 billion in grants contingent on electoral loyalty is a remarkably centralized approach to energy policy.

news.headline: Meta Pauses Plan to Charge $20/Month for Smart Glasses Feature That Runs Locally — No Cloud Required
news.summary: Metaは、スマートグラス上でローカル処理されクラウドを必要としない機能に対して月額20ドルのサブスクリプション料金を課す計画を、ユーザーの反発を受けて一時停止した。

commentary: 矛盾: クラウドサーバーを使わない、つまりMetaに継続的な運用コストがほぼ発生しない機能に対して「月額サービス料」を請求しようとしたという、サブスクリプションモデルの本質的な矛盾が露わになった。
滑稽さ: ユーザーが既に購入したハードウェア上で、ユーザー自身のバッテリーを使って動く機能に「使用料」を課すのは、購入した電灯のスイッチを押すたびに料金を取るようなものだ。
日本・海外から見ると: テック大企業が「所有」の概念を段階的に「サブスク」へ置き換えようとする動きは、消費者保護の観点から世界的に注目されている議論と重なる。
imagePrompts: A sleek pair of smart glasses displayed in a glass case with a large price tag reading '$20/month' and a small footnote label that says 'No internet required, no servers used, no cloud involved'; a confused shopper leans in to read it

A corporate boardroom with a whiteboard that reads 'COST TO US: $0 / CHARGE TO USER: $20/month'; executives in suits nod approvingly while one lone engineer in the corner holds their head in their hands

A pair of smart glasses sitting on a table with a parking meter planted next to them, the meter reading 'HEARING: 20 min / $20'; the glasses and a human ear are connected by a dotted line with no server or cloud icon anywhere in sight
captions: Meta's smart glasses are so advanced they don't need the cloud. They do, however, apparently need your credit card.
In a bold innovation, Meta found a way to monetize locally processed audio — a feature also known as 'your glasses working as designed.'
The feature runs on your glasses, uses your battery, processes on your hardware, and costs $20 a month. Meta's role in this arrangement is best described as 'billing.'
After backlash, Meta paused the plan. The glasses, unbothered, continued working fine without the subscription.
Charging $20/month for a feature that needs no server infrastructure is technically a subscription to nothing — which, in fairness, is one of Silicon Valley's most scalable business models.
captionsJa: Metaのスマートグラスはクラウドが不要なほど高性能だ。ただし、クレジットカードは必要らしい。
Metaが大胆なイノベーションを実現した。ローカル処理の音声機能を課金する方法だ。別名「グラスが仕様通りに動く機能」とも言う。
この機能はあなたのグラスで動き、あなたのバッテリーを使い、あなたのハードウェアで処理される。月額20ドルにおけるMetaの役割は、「請求書を送ること」に尽きる。
反発を受けてMetaは計画を一時停止した。グラスは動じることなく、サブスクなしで今日も快調に動き続けた。
サーバーもクラウドも不要な機能に月額20ドルを課すのは、実質「無」へのサブスクリプションだ。それがシリコンバレーで最もスケールしやすいビジネスモデルのひとつであることは、誰も否定しない。
candidates.newsEn: Meta had planned to introduce a $20 monthly subscription fee for a smart glasses feature that allows users to hear each other more clearly. The feature runs entirely on the glasses themselves and does not require cloud infrastructure or servers. After public backlash over charging for a locally processed feature, Meta confirmed it has paused the plan.

ironyEn.contradiction: Meta attempted to charge a monthly cloud fee for a feature that, by definition, uses no cloud — a creative redefinition of what 'service' means.
ironyEn.absurdity: The glasses were doing the work. The glasses' battery was doing the work. The user's ears were doing the work. Meta's contribution to this process was apparently the $20 invoice.
ironyEn.outside: Consumer advocates in Europe, already watching subscription creep closely, now have a case study in charging for the absence of a service.

ironyEn.contradiction: Silicon Valley's vision of the future is glasses that are so advanced they don't need the internet — but do apparently need a billing department.
ironyEn.absurdity: Pausing a plan that charged for locally run software after public backlash is the tech-industry equivalent of a restaurant briefly considering charging for the air conditioning before someone pointed out the diners brought their own jackets.
ironyEn.outside: International regulators pushing for right-to-repair and anti-subscription laws will find it helpful that the industry has now helpfully provided a textbook example.

news.headline: Moody's Warns 'Unprecedented' AI Spending Is Threatening the Credit Quality of Amazon, Meta, and Alphabet
news.summary: 格付け機関ムーディーズは、AI投資の急増により、世界有数のキャッシュリッチ企業であるアマゾン、Meta、アルファベットなどが大規模な借入や株式売却に頼らざるを得なくなっており、信用力に影響が出ていると警告した。

commentary: 矛盾: 「AIで業務効率を劇的に改善し、コストを削減する」と謳ってきた企業群が、そのAI開発のために人類史上類を見ない規模の借金を重ねているという皮肉な構図だ。
滑稽さ: 世界で最も現金を保有する企業たちが「資金が足りない」と言いながら、債務を積み上げてAIに注ぎ込んでいる光景は、最も裕福な子供たちがおこづかいを前借りしてゲームを買い続けているようなものだ。
日本・海外から見ると: 「AIバブル」への警戒感は世界的に高まっており、アメリカのテック大手の財務悪化は、グローバルな金融市場にも波及しうる問題として注視されている。
imagePrompts: Three enormous corporate towers labeled with recognizable tech-company colors, each with a giant wrecking ball made of dollar signs swinging through their walls, while AI robot construction workers cheer from the rubble
A Scrooge McDuck-style vault overflowing with gold coins, but with a large 'MORTGAGED' banner draped across the front and an AI server rack visible inside consuming most of the gold

A corporate earnings report on a giant screen showing a beautiful AI robot on one side and a credit rating downgrade arrow on the other, with executives in suits staring at both simultaneously with frozen smiles
captions: Congratulations to AI, which has achieved something regulators couldn't: making Amazon, Meta, and Alphabet worry about money.
The companies selling the future of efficiency are currently borrowing heavily to afford the future of efficiency.
Moody's called the AI spending 'unprecedented' — which, from a credit rating agency, is the financial equivalent of a doctor saying 'huh, interesting.'
Silicon Valley promised AI would optimize costs. It has — just for the creditors, who now get better yields.
Three of the richest companies on Earth walk into a credit warning. The punchline is that they built it themselves.
captionsJa: AIが規制当局にもできなかったことを成し遂げた。アマゾン、Meta、アルファベットに「お金の心配」をさせることだ。
「効率化の未来」を売っている企業が、「効率化の未来」を買うために多額の借金をしている。
ムーディーズはAI支出を「前例のない規模」と表現した。格付け機関からこの言葉が出ることは、医者が「ほう、これは面白い」と言うのと同じくらい良くない兆候だ。
シリコンバレーはAIがコストを最適化すると約束した。実際に最適化されたのは、債権者が得られる利回りだった。
地球上で最も裕福な3社が、そろって信用格付けの警告を受けた。オチは、その原因を自分たちで作ったということだ。
candidates.newsEn: Moody's issued a warning that the scale of AI capital expenditure is forcing even the world's most cash-rich corporations to rely heavily on debt, stock sales, and off-balance-sheet financial maneuvers. Companies including Amazon, Meta, and Alphabet are among those whose credit quality Moody's flagged as potentially at risk. The rating agency described the level of AI spending as 'unprecedented.'

ironyEn.contradiction: Companies that sell AI as the ultimate tool for efficiency and cost reduction are apparently spending so much on AI that they now need to borrow money to afford it.
ironyEn.absurdity: Amazon, Meta, and Alphabet — three of the wealthiest corporations in human history — have apparently discovered a way to spend themselves toward a credit warning.
ironyEn.outside: Global investors who were told AI would optimize everything are now watching it optimize the companies' debt-to-equity ratios in the wrong direction.

ironyEn.contradiction: The technology promising to solve humanity's resource allocation problems is, in the short term, creating a resource allocation problem for the companies building it.
ironyEn.absurdity: When the world's most cash-rich companies start needing off-balance-sheet maneuvers to fund their AI budgets, the term 'unprecedented' might be underselling it slightly.
ironyEn.outside: Regulators in Brussels and Tokyo who worried about the market dominance of U.S. tech giants can now watch Moody's do some of the work for them.

news.headline: Canadian Lawmaker Accidentally Reads AI Chatbot's Meta-Instructions Aloud on Parliament Floor
news.summary: カナダの国会議員が、議会の本会議場での演説中に、AIが生成したと見られる回答文とともに「ここに、より自然な流れの文章バージョンを示します…」というLLMの指示文をそのまま読み上げてしまった。

commentary: 矛盾: AIを使って「より自然な」スピーチを書かせた結果、最も不自然な瞬間——AIの作業指示を議場で朗読する瞬間——が生まれるという完璧な自己矛盾だ。
滑稽さ: 議会という民主主義の最も公式な場で、AIツールの舞台裏の独り言が記録として残ることになった。LLMの校閲コメントが議事録に残るのは人類史上初かもしれない。
日本・海外から見ると: 政治家がAI生成文を使うこと自体への議論はさておき、「AIの指示文ごと読んでしまう」という事故は、世界中の議会でひそかに起きているリスクを可視化した。
imagePrompts: A politician standing at a formal parliamentary podium reading from printed pages, while a giant speech bubble above shows the text including a highlighted section that reads 'Here's a more natural, flowing version of that section...' in a different font; other lawmakers in the background stare with mouths open

A close-up of a printed speech manuscript with normal text on most of the page, but one paragraph highlighted in a different color labeled 'AI EDITOR NOTE' with an arrow pointing to the podium in the background
A split image: on the left, an AI chatbot interface on a laptop screen showing a revision suggestion; on the right, the same text appearing on a parliamentary floor teleprompter while cameras roll
captions: The good news: the AI made the speech more natural. The bad news: it also included stage directions.
In a historic first, a G7 parliament's official record now contains peer review notes from a chatbot.
The AI was asked to help the legislator sound more polished. It succeeded — it's now the most memorable thing the legislator has ever said on the floor.
Transparency in government has reached new heights: we now know not just what the politician said, but also what the AI thought of the previous draft.
Somewhere, a language model has no idea it just made it into Hansard.
captionsJa: 朗報：AIがスピーチをより自然にした。悲報：AIの作業メモも一緒に読み上げた。
歴史的快挙：G7国家の議事録に、チャットボットの校閲コメントが正式記録として残ることになった。
AIは議員の言葉をより洗練させるよう依頼された。見事に成功した——議場で最も記憶に残る発言を生み出すという形で。
政府の透明性が新次元に達した。国民はその政治家が何を言ったかだけでなく、AIが前の草稿をどう評価していたかまで知ることができる。
どこかで、あるLLMが自分の下書きメモが議事録に記載されたことをまったく知らないでいる。
candidates.newsEn: A Canadian legislator delivered a floor speech that appeared to include the output of a large language model, complete with the AI's own meta-commentary. The lawmaker read aloud text that included the phrase 'Here's a more natural, flowing version of that section...' — an instruction typically generated by AI writing tools when reformatting text — apparently without noticing it was part of the model's response rather than the intended speech content.

ironyEn.contradiction: The lawmaker used AI to make the speech sound more natural, and the most memorable — and least natural — moment of the speech was generated entirely by the AI.
ironyEn.absurdity: Parliamentary records, which exist to document the words of elected officials, now include the editorial notes of a language model.
ironyEn.outside: Parliaments around the world that have debated AI transparency rules now have a case study in radical, if unintentional, transparency.

ironyEn.contradiction: The tool designed to help the politician communicate more effectively communicated, very effectively, that the politician was using the tool.
ironyEn.absurdity: Somewhere, an LLM is completely unaware that its draft notes are now part of the official legislative record of a G7 country.
ironyEn.outside: Voters who wondered how much of their representative's speech was original thought now have a data point, complete with the AI's own revision history.
